narr: A slow moving system produced thunderstorms and heavy precipitation in the Trough of Warm Air Aloft (TROWAL) region of an upper low over South Central Minnesota. Due to the prolonged duration of heavy rainfall across the region, some localities experienced localized urban flash flooding. Waseca Emergency Managment reported street and small stream flooding 3 Miles NNW of New Richland, MN as well as in town. ||Overall, the highest observed rainfall totals occurred in south central Minnesota:|St. James, MN (Watonwan): 2.90 inches of rainfall.|Madelia, MN (Watonwan): 2.58 inches of rainfall.|Hanska, MN (Brown): 2.49 inches of rainfall.|3 miles SE of Cobden (Brown): 2.42 inches of rainfall. |1 mile NW of St. James: (Watonwan): 2.15 inches of rainfall.
ev: Emergency Management in Waseca County reported that street and small stream flooding was occurring in and about three miles north of New Richland, MN. There were also reports of numerous structures and homes with flooded basements. Approximately two miles north of New Richland, a trained spotter reported that heavy rains were allowing Boot Creek to flow about six feet out of its banks and it started to run over 120th Street (Paved elevated road). Approximately three miles north of New Richland, MN, heavy rainfall caused flooding of a roadway which cut off access to a household's driveway. New Richland City Administration confirmed that flash flood waters receded within 24 hours and no longer posed a threat to public safety.
